Task: APRV-397. Follow-up filed: APRV-402 (symlinked destinations on the write pass).

## What this is

The release verification of 2026-09-20 could not run `npm pack`, `tar`, `gunzip`, `base64` or `openssl dgst` (all `hook-unclassified`), and `git tag -l` put a nine-minute `release.publish` question on the phone for a listing. Seven new classifier rows and the `git tag` read/write split.

- `npm pack` and `npm init` are workspace writes scoped like `files.write.workspace`; `--pack-destination` outside the workspace or scratch roots is refused as `files.delete.out_of_scope` (rule `packaging-write-out-of-scope`, destination bound). `npm pack <remote>` is `network.call`. `npm --version` is a read via a new `probe` matcher that matches only version and help flags, so `npm doctor` keeps its refusal.
- `tar -t` reads; `tar -x` and `tar -c` write into `-C` or the named archive path with the same scoping; `tar --version` reads; `tar` with no readable mode is opaque.
- `gunzip -c`, `-t` and `-l` read; the default form replaces the file it names and is a write. `base64` and `openssl dgst` read unless `-o`/`-out` names a file. `shasum` and `sha256sum` were already reads.
- `git tag` with `-l`, `--list`, `-n`, `--contains`, `--points-at`, `--sort`, `--format` or no arguments is `read.shell`; the read side is an allowlist, so `-a -d -f -s -m`, a bare tag name and any unlisted flag stay `release.publish` (APRV-305 intact).
- No new class. `files.write.out_of_scope` was rejected because a class no policy names would resolve by `defaults.autonomy`.

33 conformance vectors at `command-class` 1.4.0 (73 vectors, 10 controls), rule tables in the three docs, and a "Packing, unpacking and hashing" section.

For a human: SPEC section 7 introduces `files.delete.out_of_scope` as "destructive deletes outside the task's stated scope"; the classifier now also answers it for a packaging write that would overwrite outside the workspace. No normative text forbids it; a one-sentence widening of the parenthetical is proposed in the task notes and not made here.
